query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporation of 10 vol% CaF₂ nanoparticles into the CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix will form a continuous, self-lubricating CaF₂ tribofilm during sliding in air from 25 °C up to 800 °C, reducing the coefficient of friction by ≥30% and wear rate by ≥10× relative to pure CoCrFeNi across the entire temperature range.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy, as-cast and fully annealed, homogeneous microstructure
generation.intervention: Uniform dispersion of 10 vol% CaF₂ nanoparticles in the CoCrFeNi matrix via powder-metallurgy blending and hot pressing
generation.conditions: Sliding in laboratory air (21 % O₂) at temperatures of 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C; normal load = 5 N; sliding speed = 0.1 m/s; sliding distance = 1000 m per test
generation.structural_mediator: In situ–formed CaF₂ tribofilm continuous across the contact surface
generation.mechanism: Under contact stress and temperature, CaF₂ nanoparticles migrate to the sliding interface and develop a stable low-shear film that inhibits adhesive and oxidative wear, maintaining low friction and wear across the full thermal range
generation.predicted_outcome: Coefficient of friction remains below 0.4 at all tested temperatures; wear rate remains below 1×10⁻⁵ mm³/N·m at 800 °C and below 1×10⁻⁶ mm³/N·m at 25 °C, corresponding to ≥30% lower COF and ≥10× lower wear rate than pure CoCrFeNi
generation.baseline: Pure CoCrFeNi exhibits COF rising from ~0.3 at 25 °C to >0.6 at 800 °C and wear rate increasing from ~1×10⁻⁶ to ~1×10⁻⁴ mm³/N·m over the same range
generation.boundary: Valid for air environments (O₂ ~21%), normal loads between 2–10 N, sliding speeds 0.05–0.2 m/s, and temperatures 25–800 °C
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; the long-term stability and adhesion of the CaF₂ film under repeated cycling and variations in particle dispersion are not fully known

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of disk specimens: (1) pure CoCrFeNi and (2) CoCrFeNi + 10 vol% CaF₂. Perform pin-on-disk sliding tests in air at 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C under 5 N load and 0.1 m/s speed for 1000 m distance. Characterize worn tracks by friction measurement, wear volume, and surface chemistry.
measurements: Coefficient of friction vs. sliding distance
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Reject hypothesis if, at any tested temperature, the composite does not exhibit at least a 30% reduction in COF AND a 10× reduction in wear rate compared to pure CoCrFeNi.
